specification.objective: Serialize every audit event timestamp returned by GET /api/v1/audit-events as an explicit UTC instant with offset, as the time clock API already does, so the audit screen's local date/time column shows the event's real local time on every database backend.

requirements.statement: Each timestamp in the audit event list response is an ISO-8601 instant with an explicit UTC offset, including when the database driver returns a naive datetime (SQLite); stored values are interpreted as UTC, which is how the application writes them.
The audit CSV export keeps its timestamp_utc column as UTC instants ending in Z, consistent with the list response for the same event.
The frontend parses an audit timestamp with UTC offset into the same instant and renders the Data/hora (local) column in the device's local time and the UTC detail as the original UTC instant.
Audit filtering, ordering, pagination, authorization, response keys and stored audit data are unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.statement: After an audited action, every timestamp returned by GET /api/v1/audit-events parses as an offset-aware datetime with zero UTC offset that lies within the action's UTC time window.
The CSV export timestamp_utc value of an event ends in Z and denotes the same instant, to the second, as the list response timestamp of that event.

A frontend contract test parses an audit event whose timestamp ends in Z into the same instant, formats the local date/time from that instant converted to local time, and formats the UTC detail as the original instant.
The full backend and frontend suites, Flutter analysis, POLIS project gates (test.complete, lint, build, smoke), git diff check and complete diff review pass.

invariants.statement: Audit events are still stored in UTC; no schema, migration or stored value changes.
Response keys, filters, ordering, pagination, export limits and authorization of the audit API are unchanged.

forbidden_states.statement: The audit list API returns a timestamp without UTC offset.
The audit screen's local date/time column shows the UTC wall-clock time as if it were local time.

inputs.statement: AuditEvent rows whose timestamp the database driver returns either naive (SQLite) or offset-aware (PostgreSQL).

outputs.statement: Audit list JSON timestamps with explicit UTC offset, matching CSV timestamp_utc values.

failure_semantics.statement: If any audit list timestamp lacks a UTC offset or names a different instant than the CSV export, the backend regression exits nonzero naming the failing test in tests/test_audit_timestamps.py.

argv:
import shutil, subprocess, sys
flutter = shutil.which('flutter.bat') or shutil.which('flutter') or 'flutter'
backend = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', '-m', 'pytest', '-q', 'tests/test_audit_timestamps.py'], cwd='backend').returncode
frontend = subprocess.run([flutter, 'test', 'test/contracts/audit_timestamp_test.dart'], cwd='frontend').returncode
sys.exit(1 if backend or frontend else 0)
